meta.signal: WS2812 NZR 800 kbps from RP2040 PIO (T0H~350ns, T1H~700ns, bit 1.25us, exact crystal-derived timing)
meta.byte_layout: bit7=BS0 of PREVIOUS iteration, bit6=BS1 of PREVIOUS iteration, bit5..bit0=R0..R5 of THIS iteration. Chronological order within iteration i: R0..R5 at 37*i+[1,5,9,13,17,21], BS0 at 37*i+27, BS1 at 37*i+32 (stored in byte i+1 bits 7,6). First byte's bits 7..6 are garbage; the last iteration's BS0/BS1 are lost.
meta.trigger: capture starts at the first rising edge on the signal; sample R0 of iteration 0 lands ~1 cycle after the edge test fell through
meta.checksum: sum of 640 raw capture bytes mod 256
meta.trim_sweep: CLK_HSITRIMR (0x50CC) swept over codes 0..7 (3-bit trimming, default option bytes; reset value 0x00 = factory calibration). The firmware rotates the code 0,1,...,7,0,... one capture per code; the trim is applied only around cap_code (sampling runs at the trimmed clock) and restored to 0x00 before any UART output, so all UART traffic is at factory trim. The code->frequency mapping was deliberately NOT assumed; measure it from the captures.
meta.temperature: no on-chip temperature sensor (DS12129 §4.12); ambient room temperature, not instrumented
meta.trim_eps_notes: eps = relative HSI frequency error vs nominal 16 MHz, measured per capture by (t0,eps) alignment against the calibrated sampler model (synth.py constants), cross-checked with a frame-span estimate (first rise -> last fall = 191*1250+752 ns). Mapping is SIGNED 3-bit two's complement: codes 0..3 = +0..+3 steps (each step LOWERS frequency ~1.16%), codes 4..7 = -4..-1 steps (raise it). Strictly monotonic in signed order 4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3; non-monotonic in unsigned code order (wraparound jump +8.1% between codes 3 and 4). Factory (code 0) = -1.07% on this unit; code 7 (-1 step) best cancels it at +0.02%. Full authority -4.38%..+3.73%. See recon/TRIM_SWEEP.md.
